26: ///
27: /// # Accessing `MatchedPath` via extensions
28: ///
29: /// `MatchedPath` can also be accessed from middleware via request extensions.
30: ///
31: /// This is useful for example with [`Trace`](tower_http::trace::Trace) to
32: /// create a span that contains the matched path:
33: ///
34: /// ```
35: /// use axum::{
36: ///     Router,
37: ///     extract::MatchedPath,
38: ///     http::Request,
39: ///     routing::get,
40: /// };
41: /// use tower_http::trace::TraceLayer;

43: /// let app = Router::new()
44: ///     .route("/users/:id", get(|| async { /* ... */ }))
45: ///     .layer(
46: ///         TraceLayer::new_for_http().make_span_with(|req: &Request<_>| {
47: ///             let path = if let Some(path) = req.extensions().get::<MatchedPath>() {
48: ///                 path.as_str()
49: ///             } else {
50: ///                 req.uri().path()
51: ///             };
52: ///             tracing::info_span!("http-request", %path)
53: ///         }),
54: ///     );
55: /// # let _: Router = app;
56: /// ```
57: ///
58: /// # Matched path in nested routers
59: ///
60: /// Because of how [nesting] works `MatchedPath` isn't accessible in middleware on nested routes:
61: ///
62: /// ```
63: /// use axum::{
64: ///     Router,
65: ///     RequestExt,
66: ///     routing::get,
67: ///     extract::{MatchedPath, rejection::MatchedPathRejection},

74: ///     // if `/foo/bar` is called this will be `Err(_)` since that matches
75: ///     // a nested route
76: ///     let matched_path: Result<MatchedPath, MatchedPathRejection> =
77: ///         request.extract_parts::<MatchedPath>().await;
78: ///
79: ///     request
80: /// }
81: ///
82: /// // `MatchedPath` is always accessible on handlers added via `Router::route`
83: /// async fn handler(matched_path: MatchedPath) {}
84: ///
85: /// let app = Router::new()
86: ///     .nest(
87: ///         "/foo",
88: ///         Router::new().route("/bar", get(handler)),
89: ///     )
90: ///     .layer(map_request(access_matched_path));
91: /// # let _: Router = app;
92: /// ```
